instruction: Use ANSYS Workbench via the Command Line Interface (CLI) to complete a Transient Structural analysis. Physical problem: A simply supported beam is subjected to a step force at mid-span. Coordinate system and geometry: - Use the global Cartesian coordinate system. - Model the beam as a line body with a beam cross-section. - The beam reference line is along the global X direction. - The beam starts at X = 0 mm and ends at X = 1000 mm. - The mid-span location is X = 500 mm. - The beam cross section is square: - Width = 20 mm - Height = 20 mm Model parameters: - Beam length: 1000 mm - Beam cross section: 20 mm × 20 mm - Material: Structural Steel with the following properties: - Young's modulus E = 210000 MPa - Poisson's ratio ν = 0.3 - Density ρ = 7850 kg/m³ - Mesh: - Element size: 50 mm - Use 20 equal divisions along the beam length. Boundary conditions: - Left end at X = 0 mm: - Constrain UX = 0, UY = 0, and UZ = 0. - Leave rotations free. - Right end at X = 1000 mm: - Constrain UY = 0 and UZ = 0. - Leave UX free. - Leave rotations free. Load: - Apply a concentrated force at the mid-span node, X = 500 mm. - Force magnitude: 1000 N. - Force direction: negative global Y direction. - Apply the force as a step load at the start of the transient analysis and keep it constant through the analysis end time. Analysis type and settings: - Transient Structural analysis. - Enable large deflection. - Total analysis time: 0.05 s. - Time step: 0.001 s. - Save results at every time step. - Do not add structural damping. Save requirements: - Use C:\Users\user\Desktop as the working location. - Save the Workbench project file as: C:\Users\user\Desktop\wb_transient.wbpj - Save the MAPDL-equivalent database file as: C:\Users\user\Desktop\wb_transient.db - Save the MAPDL-equivalent structural result file as: C:\Users\user\Desktop\wb_transient.rst [Software] To start ANSYS Workbench, run `C:\Program Files\ANSYS Inc\v261\ansys\bin\winx64\ANSYS261.exe -g` (version/path may differ on your machine).
